title: Multiscale signed metric relations with workspace context
coverage_gap: D_N has one LL and one HH trajectory, 168 transitions in total. Their initial goal_y minus pegGrasp_y is about -0.059 and -0.049 m. The specified C and E layouts change that relation independently and can reverse its sign. Normalizing separate world coordinates on two layouts risks encoding layout identity rather than reach and insertion errors.
reusable_regularity: Direct signed hand-to-grasp and head-to-goal differences expose compositional geometry without requiring subtraction to be learned from two correlated layouts. Near-contact tanh features at 0.025 m supplement linear 0.1 m features to resolve both centimeter alignment and long-range transport. These scales are physical design constants, not measured optimal hyperparameters. Both histories use the same deterministic feature map; native state differences retain approach direction and closure dynamics. Actions remain learned entirely by the common action4 diffusion process.
dependencies_preserved: World axes, gravity, heights of hand/grasp/head/goal, and a low-gain absolute hand workspace channel are retained; no rotation or full workspace-translation symmetry is assumed.

Absolute hand position plus signed grasp-hand, head-grasp and goal-head differences reconstruct every present position, including the static box goal. Thus target/box clearance information is not discarded while emphasizing relations.
Current xyzw peg quaternion and its native previous difference preserve orientation without magnifying tiny near-constant quaternion noise with a learned support scale.

Aperture, its previous difference, hand and peg native previous displacement, and the observed inter-history pegHead displacement preserve causal motion and contact cues. The first history slot's head difference is zero because an older pegHead is not supplied.
Absent object2 channels are omitted only because common_spec declares them absent zeros. No unobserved obstacle locations or contact flags are used.

evidence_refs.detail: Exactly two complete current-support episodes and no development states.
Independent peg_y and box_y evaluation factors; world action4; separate pegGrasp and pegHead channels; fixed end-effector orientation.
LL/HH counts, 77/91 transitions, nearly identity peg quaternions, initial geometry and goal heights.
Observed rows 0-4,31-34,48-53,64-68: grasp and head differ by approximately [-0.13,0,-0.01] m; aperture decreases before lift; velocity is useful during overshoot.
Peg on table beside raised side-insertion box.
Grasp approach near table; table height cannot be quotiented out.
Peg approaches box side while held; head-to-goal rather than grasp-to-goal is an alignment cue.
Late held-peg insertion configuration in the second layout.

expected_failure_signature: If relative lifting is insufficient, grasping should remain plausible but transport lateral commands may retain the demonstrated negative-y bias in positive-offset C/E layouts.
This has no explicit manipulation-mode representation; closure/lift switches may average across similar geometric states, causing premature lift, prolonged table pressure, or stalled insertion.
Absolute workspace context allows but does not guarantee robot-boundary generalization. Extreme E layouts can still fail at reach or box clearance.

required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,42], containing only shared deployment observations
required_runtime_fields.normalization: Use raw fields for fixed physical scales, not common normalized coordinates. The common host normalizer and budget are unmodified; no fitted statistics are added.

action_frame_semantics: Identity encode/decode. First three components are native dimensionless world dx,dy,dz, scaled by 0.01 m by native control; fourth is native gripper scalar, never translated or rotated. Only the public executor clips the native cube. Horizon16 and executed prefix4 are unchanged.
loss_and_capacity: 44 conditioning features per observation, one unchanged common DP, no extra modules or auxiliary losses. Common masked action epsilon loss has weight1 and denominator mask.sum()*4.
support_fit: None; deployment_state_dict is the empty base state. No demonstration rows or phase schedules are cached.
change_summary: Initial independent model: deterministic multiscale geometric representation with identity action frame.
No optimizer updates, rollouts, performance feedback, or architecture search used in construction.
